rule: กิน files by WHO or WHAT is doing the eating. Sense 2 keeps everything a mouth or a body can take in: the feast vocabulary (กินเลี้ยง, กินบุญ, กินดอง, กินแขก), subsistence (หากิน, อยู่กิน, เก็บกิน, ของกิน), and the sexual idioms, which work only while the person is being read as food. Once the eater is not a mouth the word forks three ways — a THING that uses up a resource files at 4 (กินที่, beside the source-filed กินเวลา) or at 5 when it is an affliction eating its host (หวัดกิน, ใบ้กิน, กินตัว); a PERSON who takes something into himself files at 6 (กินเมือง takes a city, กินลม takes wind, กินแหนง takes suspicion); and a person who takes what is not owed him files at 7.

notes.text:
**กิน — the rule is WHO is doing the eating.** Sense 2 (เคี้ยวกลืน) keeps
everything a mouth or a body can take in, and that is 18 of the 34: the feast
vocabulary (กินเลี้ยง, กินบุญ, and the two wedding-feast words กินดอง and กินแขก,
which mean the same thing by two different routes — the marriage-tie ดอง, which
the dictionary gives its own Proto-Tai etymon *t.noːŋ separate from the ดอง that
is pickling, and the guests), subsistence (หากิน, อยู่กิน, เก็บกิน, ของกิน),
and the whole sexual group (กินตับ, กินเด็ก, กินไข่แดง, กินถั่วดำ), which works
only while the person is being read as food. Once the eater is not a mouth, the
word forks three ways and the three forks are the rest of the head:
